clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes EMERGENCY ADMISSION to hematology oncology unit, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: high fever, severe bleeding gums, and profound weakness over 5 days

Key HPI features: 48M presents to ED with 5-day history of high spiking fevers up to 39.5C, severe gum bleeding when brushing teeth, spontaneous petechiae across both shins, and extreme fatigue. Denies cough, dysuria, or recent travel.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 39.4C, HR 118, BP 104/64. Pallor, petechiae on lower extremities, oozing gingiva. Bloods: WBC 45,000 /uL with 75% circulating blasts, Hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL, Platelets 14,000 /uL. Peripheral blood smear reveals large myeloblasts containing distinct Auer rods. Coagulation screen: PT and PTT slightly elevated, Fibrinogen 120 mg/dL (mild DIC risk).
Relevant background/PMH: No prior chronic illness
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Aplastic anemia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: High fever with suspected low white count (neutropenic fever) — a hematologic emergency.
management_principles: EMERGENCY ADMISSION to hematology oncology unit
Immediate broad-spectrum empiric IV antibiotics (Cefepime 2g q8h) after blood cultures for febrile neutropenia
Transfuse irradiated single-donor platelets (keep >20,000 due to bleeding) and packed RBCs
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: high fever, severe bleeding gums, and profound weakness over 5 days

48M presents to ED with 5-day history of high spiking fevers up to 39.5C, severe gum bleeding when brushing teeth, spontaneous petechiae across both shins, and extreme fatigue. Denies cough, dysuria, or recent travel.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 39.4C, HR 118, BP 104/64. Pallor, petechiae on lower extremities, oozing gingiva. Bloods: WBC 45,000 /uL with 75% circulating blasts, Hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL, Platelets 14,000 /uL. Peripheral blood smear reveals large myeloblasts containing distinct Auer rods. Coagulation screen: PT and PTT slightly elevated, Fibrinogen 120 mg/dL (mild DIC risk).
reference_soap.assessment: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) presenting with febrile neutropenia and symptomatic cytopenias.
reference_soap.plan: EMERGENCY ADMISSION to hematology oncology unit. 1. Immediate broad-spectrum empiric IV antibiotics (Cefepime 2g q8h) after blood cultures for febrile neutropenia. 2. Transfuse irradiated single-donor platelets (keep >20,000 due to bleeding) and packed RBCs. 3. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy with flow cytometry/cytogenetics for AML subtyping. Prepare for induction chemotherapy (7+3 regimen: Cytarabine + Daunorubicin).

learning_objectives: Recognize hematologic emergencies requiring immediate resuscitation (febrile neutropenia, acute bleeding)
Identify Auer rods on peripheral smear as diagnostic hallmark of myeloblasts in AML
Execute febrile neutropenia empiric antibiotic protocol within 60 minutes of arrival
Manage acute transfusion thresholds for thrombocytopenia and anemia in leukemia patients

teaching.one_liner: A bone-marrow cancer that crowds out normal blood cell production, causing the triad of infection risk (low white cells), bleeding (low platelets), and fatigue (low red cells) all at once.
red_flags: High fever with suspected low white count (neutropenic fever) — a hematologic emergency

must_ask.say: How many days have you had the fever and bleeding gums?
Besides your gums, have you noticed any other unusual bleeding or bruising?
How high has your fever been, and does it come and go?
How is the extreme tiredness affecting your daily activities?
Any cough, pain when urinating, or other signs of infection?
What worries you most about these symptoms?
